display.title: Tanya Shiur 51, Part 2: Chapter 32, Ahavas Yisroel and Unity
display.summary_short: The second half of a Yiddish Tanya shiur on chapter 32: why love for every Jew is the root of the Torah, and how the Shechinah rests only where Jews are united.
display.summary_long: The second half of Rabbi Yosef Goldstein's Yiddish shiur on Tanya chapter 32, cut from the full recording of that class. It opens with Hillel's teaching that 'love your fellow as yourself' is the whole Torah: the root of the Torah is raising the soul above the body and drawing Hashem's light to the source of all Jewish souls, so Jews must stand united. The Shechinah rests only in a complete place, as we pray 'bless us, our Father, all of us as one'. A chain of bar mitzvah questions among the Chabad Rebbeim explains why the Siddur has us accept this mitzvah before davening: like a gift brought before asking a king for something. The Rebbe's teaching about Shemini Atzeres, 'your parting is hard for Me', shows Hashem's pain when Jews are divided. One cannot truly love Hashem while hating a Jew, who is a part of Him. The class ends with how to relate to a Jew who sins: after rebuke, hate the deed but love the person, and keep working to bring him close.
display.lesson: The way to love Hashem and to bring His presence is to love every Jew; even toward one who sins, hate only the deed and keep loving the person.
